from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Two blocks slide on a frictionless surface.",
            "They collide with each other and the wall.",
            "Counting collisions mysteriously reveals digits of pi.",
            "A mouse block hits an elephant block.",
            "Let's count these mechanical impacts!"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Impossible Counting Puzzle", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        mouse = Square(side_length=0.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        elephant = Square(side_length=1.5, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5)
        blocks = VGroup(mouse, elephant).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(blocks, 'C2')
        self.play(FadeIn(blocks))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        wall = Line(start=UP*2, end=DOWN*2, color=GRAY, stroke_width=10)
        self.place_at_grid(wall, 'C5')
        self.play(Create(wall))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        pi_symbol = MathTex(r"\pi", color=YELLOW, font_size=72)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_symbol, 'A3')
        self.play(Write(pi_symbol))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        mouse_label = Text("Mouse", font_size=18).next_to(mouse, UP)
        elephant_label = Text("Elephant", font_size=18).next_to(elephant, UP)
        self.add(mouse_label, elephant_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=96, color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(question_mark, scale=2))
        self.play(Indicate(blocks))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Mechanical systems reveal fundamental mathematical constants.",
            "Symmetry and conservation govern our universe.",
            "100^n collisions count n digits."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Recap principles
        recaps = VGroup(
            Text("Conservation of Energy", font_size=24, color="#00FF00"),
            Text("Elastic Collisions", font_size=24, color="#00FF00"),
            Text("Phase Space Geometry", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(recaps, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(recaps))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Connection
        conn = Text("Phase Space = Pi", font_size=32, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(conn, "D3")
        self.play(Flash(conn, color="#FFD700"), Write(conn))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Infographic
        info = VGroup(
            Text("1 coll. -> 3", font_size=24, color="#87CEEB"),
            Text("100 coll. -> 3.1", font_size=24, color="#87CEEB"),
            Text("10,000 coll. -> 3.14", font_size=24, color="#87CEEB")
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(info, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(info))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#87CEEB")
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Fade out
        self.play(FadeOut(recaps), FadeOut(conn), FadeOut(info))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Pi-Collision Mystery: Counting Collisions to Calculate Digits of Pi
outline.target_audience: High school students or curious science enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: The Impossible Counting Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle: Two blocks of mass m and M = 100^n * m sliding on a frictionless surface. We count collisions between the two blocks and the wall. Present the counter-intuitive claim: the total number of collisions equals the first n digits of pi.
sections.example: Visualize two blocks: a small 'Mouse' block (m=1kg) and a massive 'Elephant' block (M=100kg) heading towards a wall.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly explain the Elastic Collision framework. We use the Conservation of Momentum and Kinetic Energy to track block velocities. This provides the 'logic' behind why blocks bounce back and forth.
sections.example: A simple 1D animation showing a ball hitting a wall and reversing velocity, then hitting another ball and transferring energy.

sections.title: The Geometry of Phase Space
sections.content: Transition from 1D motion to 2D geometry. By plotting the velocities of the two blocks as coordinates (v1, v2) on a graph, we show that the collision process traces an arc of a circle. This is the 'Aha!' moment where physics becomes geometry.
sections.example: An animation transforming the 'back-and-forth' collision motion into a bouncing 'ball' inside a circular arc on a Cartesian plane.

sections.title: Unveiling the Pi Connection
sections.content: Explain that as the mass ratio M/m increases (powers of 100), the number of collisions is effectively dividing the circumference of a circle by the length of the arc defined by the collision angle, which relates to the arcsin function, leading directly to the digits of pi.
sections.example: A visual overlay where the trajectory of the 'system state' hits a boundary exactly enough times to map out 3.14...

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Synthesize the concept: Why does a mechanical puzzle generate a transcendental number? Reinforce that symmetry and conservation laws govern not just physics, but the fundamental constants of mathematics.
sections.example: A final infographic showing: 1 collision = 3, 100 collisions = 31, 10,000 collisions = 314.
